ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, $CD$ is the height on the hypotenuse $AB$, $AD=3$, then what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since CD$\perp$AB and $\angle$ACB=$90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$ADC=$90^\circ=\angle$ACB,\\
since $\angle$B=$30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$A$=90^\circ-\angle$B$=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle$ACD$=90^\circ-\angle$A$=30^\circ$,\\
since AD$=3$,\\
it follows that AC$=2$AD$=6$,\\
thus AB$=2$AC$=12$,\\
hence BD$=AB-AD$=$12-3$=$\boxed{9}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, and AB as the horizontal base; C is above, and a right-angle symbol is marked at C, indicating ∠ACB = 90°. Point D is located on AB, and segment CD drops perpendicularly from C to AB; a right-angle symbol is also marked at D, so CD is the altitude to the hypotenuse AB; AD is a segment on the left side of AB, and BD is a segment on the right side of AB. The problem gives ∠B = 30°, AD = 3. Reasoning: In right triangle ABC, ∠ACB = 90°, ∠B = 30°, so ∠A = 60°. In right triangle ACD, ∠D = 90°, and ∠A = 60°, therefore ∠ACD = 30°. At this time AC is the hypotenuse of triangle ACD, and AD is the side opposite the 30° angle; in a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, the hypotenuse is equal to 2 times the side opposite the 30° angle, so AC = 2AD = 2 × 3 = 6. In the original triangle ABC, ∠B = 30°, AC is the side opposite the 30° angle, and AB is the hypotenuse, so AB = 2AC = 12. Thus BD = AB − AD = 12 − 3 = 9.
